Computer Science and Engineering is one of the most popular courses among engineering students. It mainly focuses on programming, computation, analysis of algorithms, program design and testing, and software engineering for the design, development, and analysis of software and hardware used to solve the problems of various businesses, scientific, and social issues. Computer Science and Engineering integrates both computer hardware and software, intending to develop a solid understanding of the entire computer system, its accessories, and software. It provides sophistication to the world and touches human lives in all aspects, such as education, transportation, entertainment, banking, social media, healthcare, and supply chain management. This field is an interdisciplinary subject incorporating elements from psychology, geology, science, mathematics, art, music, bioinformatics, electronics, and operations research. The study helps students understand how computer science fits into a wide range of domains in the world.

The program offered is a B.E. in Computer Science and Engineering, with a duration of four years for regular students and three years for lateral entry students. The regular program consists of eight semesters, while the lateral entry program has six semesters. The total intake is 60 seats, divided equally between the government quota and the management quota. Eligibility for the program requires completion of the 10+2 system of education, and students must have secured a pass in Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics in their qualifying examination. The curriculum and syllabus fall under the 2021 Regulation and the 2017 Regulation.

Career opportunities for graduates include roles as planners, designers, constructors, and operators. They can also work as stewards of the environment, innovators and integrators of technology, managers of risk, and leaders in public policy. Opportunities are abundant in public sector undertakings and government sectors. The scope for higher studies is excellent, with graduates often pursuing an M.E., M.Tech, or M.B.A. **MSAJCEA** specifically offers an M.E. in Computer Science and Engineering for those looking to advance their technical education.

NATIONAL ASSESSMENT AND ACCREDITATION COUNCIL (NAAC)

India boasts one of the largest and most diverse education systems globally, with significant advancements in recent years. The introduction of new and emerging programs, increased autonomy, and widespread expansion have collectively improved access to higher education. However, these developments have also raised concerns regarding the quality and relevance of higher education. In response to these concerns, the National Policy on Education (NPE) was introduced in 1986, followed by the Programme of Action (PoA) in 1992, which outlined strategic plans for addressing these issues and advocated for the establishment of an independent national accreditation agency.

Consequently, the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) was established in 1994 as an autonomous institution under the University Grants Commission (UGC), with its headquarters located in Bengaluru. The NAAC's vision statement reflects its core mandate, which is to integrate quality assurance into the functioning of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), thereby ensuring a commitment to excellence in education.

The National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) operates through two key bodies: the General Council (GC) and the Executive Committee (EC), both of which comprise a diverse group of educational administrators, policymakers, and senior academicians from various segments of the Indian higher education system.

At the helm of the NAAC's General Council is the Chairperson of the University Grants Commission (UGC), who serves as the President of the GC. The Chairperson of the Executive Committee, on the other hand, is an esteemed academician nominated by the President of the GC. This nomination process ensures that the EC is led by a highly respected and knowledgeable individual in the field of education.

The Director of the NAAC plays a pivotal role in the organization, serving as both the academic and administrative head. In addition to these responsibilities, the Director is also the member secretary of both the General Council and the Executive Committee, facilitating the smooth functioning of these bodies.

Beyond its statutory bodies and core staff, the NAAC also seeks guidance from advisory and consultative committees that are constituted as needed. These committees provide valuable insights and expertise, enabling the NAAC to make informed decisions and develop effective policies.

Under Model 1, the Computer Science and Engineering sector offers a Computer Hardware Network Maintenance course for the job role of Computer Hardware Network Maintenance with an approved intake of 30, an NSQF level of 4, and 1600 hours. The Mechanical Engineering sector offers a Refrigeration And Air Conditioning Technician course with an approved intake of 30, an NSQF level of 5, and 3200 hours.

Under Model 2, the Computer Science and Engineering sector offers an AI Machine learning Developer course with an approved intake of 30, an NSQF level of 7, and 756 hours. The Mechanical Engineering sector offers a Refrigeration And Air Conditioning Technician course with an approved intake of 30, an NSQF level of 5, and 3200 hours. The Mechanical Engineering sector also offers an Additive Manufacturing Technician in 3D Printing course with an approved intake of 30, an NSQF level of 4, and 2080 hours. The Electronics Engineering sector offers a Certificate Course in Embedded System Design using ARM or Cortex Microcontroller with an approved intake of 30, an NSQF level of 5, and 80 hours. The Architecture Engineering sector offers an Architectural Drafting and Basic 3D Design with Autodesk Revit course with an approved intake of 30, an NSQF level of 4, and 500 hours. Admissions & Eligibility: ### Document: Admissions & Eligibility | Section: Programmes Offered and Seats Available — 1. Under Graduate Programmes

**MSAJCEA** offers various Under Graduate programmes with a total sanctioned intake for each course divided equally between the Government Quota and the Management Quota. For B.E. Civil Engineering, the total sanctioned intake is 30 seats, with 15 seats under the Government Quota and 15 seats under the Management Quota. For B.E. Computer Science and Engineering, which has permanent affiliation, the total sanctioned intake is 60 seats, with 30 seats for Government Quota and 30 seats for Management Quota. For B.E. Electronics and Communication Engineering, the total intake is 60 seats, split as 30 for Government Quota and 30 for Management Quota. For B.E. Electrical and Electronics Engineering, the total intake is 30 seats, with 15 seats for Government Quota and 15 for Management Quota. For B.E. Mechanical Engineering, which also has permanent affiliation, the total intake is 30 seats, with 15 seats for Government Quota and 15 for Management Quota. For B.Tech. Information Technology, the total intake is 60 seats, with 30 seats for Government Quota and 30 for Management Quota. For B.Tech. Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, the total intake is 60 seats, with 30 seats for Government Quota and 30 for Management Quota. For B.Tech. Computer Science and Business Systems, the total intake is 30 seats, with 15 seats for Government Quota and 15 for Management Quota. For B.E. Computer Science and Engineering in Cyber Security, the total intake is 30 seats, with 15 seats for Government Quota and 15 for Management Quota. For B.Tech. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, the total intake is 60 seats, with 30 seats for Government Quota and 30 for Management Quota. For B.Tech. Electronics Engineering with specialisation in VLSI Design and Technology, the total intake is 30 seats, with 15 seats for Government Quota and 15 for Management Quota. For B.Tech. ECE with specialisation in Advanced Communication Technology, the total intake is 30 seats, with 15 seats for Government Quota and 15 for Management Quota. For Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch.), the total intake is 40 seats, with 20 seats for Government Quota and 20 for Management Quota. For Bachelor of Design (B.Des.), the total intake is 30 seats, with 15 seats for Government Quota and 15 for Management Quota. Five percent of seats within the Approved Intake shall be allowed for admission under the NRI category, and in the event of non-availability of students in NRI seats, the seats shall be given to general candidates as per merit. Admissions & Eligibility: ### Document: Admissions & Eligibility | Section: Programmes Offered and Seats Available — 2. Post Graduate Programmes

**MSAJCEA** offers Post Graduate programmes where the total sanctioned intake is divided between Government and Management Quotas. For Computer Science and Engineering, the total sanctioned intake is 9 seats, with 3 seats under the Government Quota and 6 seats under the Management Quota. For Structural Engineering, the total intake is 18 seats, with 6 seats for Government Quota and 12 for Management Quota. For Master of Architecture, the total intake is 15 seats, with 7 seats for Government Quota and 8 for Management Quota. Five percent of seats within the Approved Intake shall be allowed for admission under the NRI category, and in the event of non-availability of students in NRI seats, the seats shall be given to general candidates as per merit. Admissions & Eligibility: ### Document: Admissions & Eligibility | Section: Programmes Offered and Seats Available — 11. Undergraduate Scholarships

The Pragati scholarship scheme for Girl Students, funded by AICTE, requires a maximum of two girl children per family and an income of less than 8 Lakh. The scholarship amount is 50000 rupees per year, with 800 scholarships for Tamil Nadu. The Saksham scholarship scheme for specially abled students, funded by AICTE, requires a disability of not less than 40 percent and an income of less than 8 Lakh. The scholarship amount is 50000 rupees per year, and all eligible candidates in Tamil Nadu can receive it. The Merit cum based Scholarship for the minority community only, funded by the Ministry of Minority Affairs, requires 50 percent marks in the final examination and an income of less than 2.5 Lakh. The scholarship amount is 20000 rupees per year, plus 12000 for hostellers and 6000 for day scholars, with 1075 scholarships for Muslims and 1173 for Christians in Tamil Nadu. The Central Sector Scheme, funded by MHRD, requires 80 percent marks in the final examination and an income of less than 8 Lakh. The scholarship amount is 10000 rupees per year, with 4883 scholarships for Tamil Nadu. Financial Assistance for Education to the wards of Beedi, Mine, and Cine workers, funded by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, requires an income of less than 10000 per month. The scholarship amount is 15000 rupees per year, and all eligible candidates in Tamil Nadu can receive it.

gold_answer: 8 semesters
actual_answer:
Based on verified MSAJCE official records: Admissions & Eligibility: ### Document: Admissions & Eligibility | Section: Programmes Offered and Seats Available — 8. Postgraduate M.E and M.Tech Admission Eligibility

For the two-year M.E or M.Tech Degree Programmes, the qualification for admission to M.E in Computer Science and Engineering requires a B.E or B.Tech in EEE, ECE, CSE, IT, I and C, E and I, IT, Electronics, or Instrumentation, or an M.C.A or an M.Sc 5 years integrated in IT, CSE, or Software Engineering in a 10 plus 2 plus 3 plus 3 years pattern. The qualification for admission to M.E in Structural Engineering requires a B.E Degree in Civil Engineering. For M.E Courses, students are admitted by **MSAJCEA** as per Government rules and regulations on the basis of the marks obtained by the candidates in their qualifying examinations. The candidates can be admitted through the Tamil Nadu Common Entrance Test conducted by Anna University. Admissions & Eligibility: ### Document: Admissions & Eligibility | Section: Programmes Offered and Seats Available — 7. Direct Second Year Lateral Entry Eligibility

For Direct Second Year Lateral Entry Degree Courses, Diploma Candidates must have a pass with prescribed minimum eligibility marks in any one of the Diploma in appropriate branch of Engineering or Technology of the State Board of Technical Education and Training, Tamil Nadu or equivalent prescribed for admission to the Degree Course. B.Sc. Candidates must have a pass with prescribed minimum eligibility marks in any recognized Bachelor’s Degree in Science of minimum 3 years duration with 10 plus 2 plus 3 years pattern and studied core Mathematics as one of the subjects at degree level. Candidates with a Degree other than Bachelor of Science are not eligible. For any clarification with regard to Diploma qualification, students should write a letter to DOTE to get it clarified. On any account, candidates without prescribed qualifications will not be given admission approval. 

Both Diploma and B.Sc. qualified candidates have to obtain the following minimum eligibility marks for admission to Lateral Entry. For the General Category, a pass with a minimum average mark of 55 percent is required. For the Backward Class including Backward Class Muslim, a pass with a minimum average mark of 50 percent is required. For the MBC and DNC categories, a pass with a minimum average mark of 45 percent is required. For the SC, SCA, and ST categories, a mere pass in the qualifying examination for Diploma examinations as stipulated by the State Board of Technical Education and Training, Tamil Nadu or B.Sc. For the Ph.D Degree in Mechanical Engineering, candidates must have a Master's Degree or any other qualification recognized as equivalent thereto in the fields of study notified from time to time by Anna University. Specifically, they must hold an M.E, M.Tech, or M.S By Research in the relevant branch of Engineering or Technology. Candidates should have the required qualification in the order of studies 10th, HSC, UG, and PG degree or its equivalent qualification. Alternatively, a Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or Technology of the University or any other qualification recognized as equivalent thereto in the fields of study with a minimum of 15 years of R and D Experience in National Research Laboratories or Public sector undertakings and with a minimum of three publications in referred impact factor journals or two approved international patents in the last five years is accepted. A minimum of 55 percent marks or a CGPA of 5.5 on a 10 point scale in the qualifying examination is required. In the case of SC, ST, or Differently-Abled candidates, 50 percent marks or a CGPA of 5.0 on a 10 point scale is required. Based on verified MSAJCE official records: E-Governance & Service Policies: ### Document: E-Governance & Service Policies | Section: Scholarship Policy

Mohamed Sathak Educational Trust Scholarship: Mohamed Sathak educational trust provides merit scholarship to the eligible students, throughout their course of study to support their education as per the following criteria: Students who willing to join in **MSAJCEA** with cut-off mark of 180 and above out of 200 marks will be considered as eligible students to acquire the merit scholarship and it is provided only to the students those who get approval from **MSAJCEA** before attending the counseling. Students who are from underprivileged background, despite their aggregate marks. (Evident with the income certificate). Special consideration of up to 10% in tuition fees for the girls students. The following processes need to adhere to claim the merit scholarship: The students who are eligible have to fill an application form and the same has to be submitted to the Administration Office. The Scholarship committee will verify the authenticity of the certificates through a transparent approach and subsequently recommend the students to the trust for providing the eligible scholarship. A certificate denoting their Scholarship throughout their course of study will be provided as a documentary to the Scholarship availed students. All the students should maintain their academic credentials and disciplined to continue the scholarship. Government Scholarships: College creates awareness and assists students in applying for scholarships provided by Central & State government under various schemes. Name of the Scheme Funding Agency Scholarship Amount in Rs Pragati scholarship scheme for Girl Students AICTE Rs. 50,000 per year Saksham scholarship scheme for specially abled students AICTE Rs. 50,000 per year Merit cum based Scholarship ( minority community only) Ministry of Minority Affairs Rs. 20,000 per year + Rs. 12000 for Hosteller, Rs. 6000 for Day Scholar Central Sector Scheme MHRD Rs. 10000 per year Financial Assistance for Education to the wards of Beedi/Mine/Cine workers Ministry of Labor & Employment Rs. 15000 per year PRINCIPAL Admissions & Eligibility: ### Document: Admissions & Eligibility | Section: Programmes Offered and Seats Available — 11. Undergraduate Scholarships

The Pragati scholarship scheme for Girl Students, funded by AICTE, requires a maximum of two girl children per family and an income of less than 8 Lakh. The scholarship amount is 50000 rupees per year, with 800 scholarships for Tamil Nadu. The Saksham scholarship scheme for specially abled students, funded by AICTE, requires a disability of not less than 40 percent and an income of less than 8 Lakh. The scholarship amount is 50000 rupees per year, and all eligible candidates in Tamil Nadu can receive it. The Merit cum based Scholarship for the minority community only, funded by the Ministry of Minority Affairs, requires 50 percent marks in the final examination and an income of less than 2.5 Lakh. The scholarship amount is 20000 rupees per year, plus 12000 for hostellers and 6000 for day scholars, with 1075 scholarships for Muslims and 1173 for Christians in Tamil Nadu. The Central Sector Scheme, funded by MHRD, requires 80 percent marks in the final examination and an income of less than 8 Lakh. The scholarship amount is 10000 rupees per year, with 4883 scholarships for Tamil Nadu. Financial Assistance for Education to the wards of Beedi, Mine, and Cine workers, funded by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, requires an income of less than 10000 per month. The scholarship amount is 15000 rupees per year, and all eligible candidates in Tamil Nadu can receive it. For Direct Second Year Lateral Entry Degree Courses, Diploma Candidates must have a pass with prescribed minimum eligibility marks in any one of the Diploma in appropriate branch of Engineering or Technology of the State Board of Technical Education and Training, Tamil Nadu or equivalent prescribed for admission to the Degree Course. B.Sc. Candidates must have a pass with prescribed minimum eligibility marks in any recognized Bachelor’s Degree in Science of minimum 3 years duration with 10 plus 2 plus 3 years pattern and studied core Mathematics as one of the subjects at degree level. Candidates with a Degree other than Bachelor of Science are not eligible. For any clarification with regard to Diploma qualification, students should write a letter to DOTE to get it clarified. On any account, candidates without prescribed qualifications will not be given admission approval. 

Both Diploma and B.Sc. qualified candidates have to obtain the following minimum eligibility marks for admission to Lateral Entry. For the General Category, a pass with a minimum average mark of 55 percent is required. For the Backward Class including Backward Class Muslim, a pass with a minimum average mark of 50 percent is required. For the MBC and DNC categories, a pass with a minimum average mark of 45 percent is required. For the SC, SCA, and ST categories, a mere pass in the qualifying examination for Diploma examinations as stipulated by the State Board of Technical Education and Training, Tamil Nadu or B.Sc. Degree examinations or equivalent is required. When candidates produce a grade certificate, they have to produce the actual marks also, otherwise only the minimum marks applicable to the grades in the subjects will be taken into account.

The B.Tech program in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science provides a comprehensive education in these rapidly growing fields. Artificial intelligence is the process of creating machines to think like humans. It is a term used to describe the simulation of human intelligence processes in machines. It typically involves sophisticated algorithms that enable computers to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence, such as visual perception, speech recognition, and decision making.

Data Science is a field of knowledge which applies advanced statistical and mathematical techniques to large datasets in order to extract knowledge from them. This data can be structured like a spreadsheet but can also be unstructured like text or video data. Data science is the application of techniques from statistics, mathematics, computer programming, and other fields to solve real-world problems using information technology.

Due to the exploration of the Internet, Artificial Intelligence and Data Science deliver data-driven solutions using computational principles, methods, and systems for extracting information from data and modern computational systems that reveal capabilities of insight, way of thinking, learning, and action that are typical of human intelligence.

Since 2015, the B.Tech in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science has emerged as one of the most high-growth, dynamic, and lucrative careers in technology. This course aims at providing not only the core technologies such as artificial intelligence, data mining, and data modeling but also gives intensive inputs in areas of machine learning and big data analytics. Through this course, the students will gain cross-disciplinary skills across fields such as statistics, computer science, machine learning, and logic. Graduates may have career opportunities in healthcare, business, e-commerce, social networking companies, climatology, biotechnology, genetics, and other important areas. The major focus of this programme is to equip students with statistical, mathematical reasoning, machine learning, knowledge discovery, and visualization skills.

Electronics & Communication (ECE): ### Document: Electronics & Communication (ECE) | Section: Electronics and Communication Engineering — 7. Programme Outcomes (PO)

The Programme Outcomes define the foundational abilities of the students. - **Programme Outcome (PO1) - Engineering Knowledge**: Engineering knowledge requires applying mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to solve complex engineering problems. Problem analysis involves identifying, formulating, reviewing research literature, and analyzing complex engineering problems to reach substantiated conclusions. For the design and development of solutions, students must design solutions for complex engineering problems that meet specified needs with appropriate consideration for public health and safety, as well as cultural, societal, and environmental considerations. Conducting investigations of complex problems requires using research-based knowledge and methods, including the design of experiments, analysis, and interpretation of data to provide valid conclusions. Modern tool usage involves creating, selecting, and applying appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools, including prediction and modeling, to complex engineering activities.

Further Programme Outcomes emphasize the engineer and society, applying reasoning informed by contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal, and cultural issues relevant to professional engineering practice. Environment and sustainability focus on understanding the impact of professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts. - **Programme Outcome (PO8) - Ethics**: Ethics involves applying ethical principles and committing to professional ethics, responsibilities, and norms of engineering practice. - **Programme Outcome (PO9) - Individual and Team Work**: Individual and teamwork require functioning effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams and multidisciplinary settings. Communication ensures the ability to communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and society at large. Project management and finance involve demonstrating knowledge and understanding of engineering and management principles. - **Programme Outcome (PO12) - Life-long Learning**: Finally, life-long learning recognizes the need for and the ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change. Based on verified MSAJCE official records: ECE - VLSI Design & Technology: ### Document: ECE - VLSI Design & Technology | Section: Electronics Engineering with Specialization in VLSI Design and Technology — 1. Overview | Version: 2026-27
A serious crunch is observed in the trained manpower in every aspect of the semiconductor ecosystem in the country. Various schemes and policies are framed by the Government of India to encourage start-ups, MSMEs, industries, and large business houses, including the Chips to Startup programme of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. It is estimated that the total manpower requirement over the next five to seven years will be around 85,000 across undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral levels in the fields of VLSI Technology, Semiconductor Manufacturing, Electronics, Electrical, Mechanical, and Chemical Engineering. The Government of India announced a Semiconductor scheme with a massive outlay to fulfill the Aatma Nirbhar Bharath vision and contribute significantly to the global semiconductor market.

**MSAJCEA** is dedicated to becoming a part of this endeavor to create the human resources required for the semiconductor industry in the upcoming years by providing trained engineers through the National Semiconductor Mission. The outcome of this program is to improve the world through transformative education and impactful research by producing outstanding graduates who are knowledgeable, creative, and passionate about building a vibrant semiconductor and display ecosystem to enable India’s emergence as a global hub for electronics manufacturing and design.

B.Tech in Electronics Engineering with Specialization in VLSI Design and Technology is offered in the Faculty of Electronics and Communication Engineering. VLSI is the process of designing and manufacturing integrated circuits. The VLSI design curriculum emphasizes the key aspects of software and hardware design and development of VLSI applications such as device modeling, RF circuit design, testing and diagnosis of VLSI circuits, VLSI signal processing, chip packaging, system design verification, and system on chip. VLSI Design and its applications are found in areas like signal processing, image processing, networks and communication applications, space applications, and quantum computing. This programme aims to cater to the exponential rise in demand for a semiconductor talent pool in India and across the globe, preparing market-ready engineers for the semiconductor technology and electronics industries. ECE - VLSI Design & Technology: ### Document: ECE - VLSI Design & Technology | Section: Electronics Engineering with Specialization in VLSI Design and Technology — 1. Overview | Version: 2026-27
The B.Tech in Electronics Engineering with Specialization in VLSI Design and Technology addresses the exponential demand for integrated chips and sensors driven by the proliferation of the digital economy and consumer electronics. Meeting this burgeoning domestic demand is challenging as India currently imports integrated chips in billions of US dollars. The post-COVID global semiconductor market has grown exponentially and is expected to reach one trillion dollars by 2030, driven by technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Electric Vehicles, 5G Networks, the Internet of Things, and Health Care. Realization of these technologies depends on the production of silicon chips, leading to the establishment of many chip-making industries in research and development, design, manufacturing, and testing to fill the gap in the chip supply chain. Overall semiconductor import has surpassed that of gold, standing second only to crude oil, and the deficit is expected to rise further from a long-term economic perspective. Hence, the existing gap must be bridged by realizing indigenous manufacturing of integrated chips.

Most of the tape-out is currently being siliconized in foreign countries since India has only a single Integrated Design to Manufacturing pilot line at the Semi-Conductor Laboratory based on the 180nm Node. Recently, the Government of India has given impetus to the Electronics System Design and Manufacturing policy for full-flow custom design solutions. Foundries and companies are encouraged to set up chip manufacturing units under the Indian Semiconductor Mission to build vibrant ecosystems of semiconductor and display systems. A common concern associated with setting up and running a commercial fab in India is the availability of trained manpower required to run the system. Quality assurance is a by-product of ongoing efforts to define the objectives of an institution, to have a work plan to achieve them and to specify the checks and balances to evaluate the degree to which each of the tasks is fulfilled. Hence devotion and commitment to improvement rather than mere institutional control is the basis for devising procedures and instruments for assuring quality. The right balance between the health and growth of an institution needs to be struck. The IQAC has to ensure that whatever is done in **MSAJCEA** for education is done efficiently and effectively with high standards. In order to do this, the IQAC will have to first establish procedures and modalities to collect data and information on various aspects of institutional functioning. The coordinators of the IQAC and the secretary have a major role in implementing these functions. The IQAC may derive major support from the already existing units and mechanisms that contribute to the listed functions. The Mohamed Sathak A.J. **MSAJCEA** campus sprawls over 70 acres of greenery located inside the SIPCOT IT Park in Siruseri, and it is surrounded by multinational IT companies such as TCS, CTS, Intellect, Aspire, Steria, Polaris, and FSS. **MSAJCEA** has good infrastructure facilities such as spacious classrooms, drawing halls, laboratories, seminar halls, computer facilities with internet and wifi connectivity, a library, workshops, an auditorium, and a playground. **MSAJCEA** is well connected by road, rail, and air from various parts of the country. - **Food Streets**: The **Navalur Junction** and **Thazhambur Main Road** are lined with hundreds of restaurants, ranging from quick-service (McDonald's, KFC, Domino's) to fine dining.

A home away from home is provided for both boys and girls separately. All the rooms are well furnished with modern amenities such as cot, mattress with pillows, bed-spreads, individual cup-boards, chair-table with lamp, fan, water heater, and wall hangers.

The Pragati scholarship scheme for Girl Students, funded by AICTE, requires a maximum of two girl children per family and an income of less than 8 Lakh. The scholarship amount is 50000 rupees per year, with 800 scholarships for Tamil Nadu. The Saksham scholarship scheme for specially abled students, funded by AICTE, requires a disability of not less than 40 percent and an income of less than 8 Lakh. The scholarship amount is 50000 rupees per year, and all eligible candidates in Tamil Nadu can receive it. The Merit cum based Scholarship for the minority community only, funded by the Ministry of Minority Affairs, requires 50 percent marks in the final examination and an income of less than 2.5 Lakh. The scholarship amount is 20000 rupees per year, plus 12000 for hostellers and 6000 for day scholars, with 1075 scholarships for Muslims and 1173 for Christians in Tamil Nadu. The Central Sector Scheme, funded by MHRD, requires 80 percent marks in the final examination and an income of less than 8 Lakh. The scholarship amount is 10000 rupees per year, with 4883 scholarships for Tamil Nadu. Financial Assistance for Education to the wards of Beedi, Mine, and Cine workers, funded by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, requires an income of less than 10000 per month. For Direct Second Year Lateral Entry Degree Courses, Diploma Candidates must have a pass with prescribed minimum eligibility marks in any one of the Diploma in appropriate branch of Engineering or Technology of the State Board of Technical Education and Training, Tamil Nadu or equivalent prescribed for admission to the Degree Course. B.Sc. Candidates must have a pass with prescribed minimum eligibility marks in any recognized Bachelor’s Degree in Science of minimum 3 years duration with 10 plus 2 plus 3 years pattern and studied core Mathematics as one of the subjects at degree level. Candidates with a Degree other than Bachelor of Science are not eligible. For any clarification with regard to Diploma qualification, students should write a letter to DOTE to get it clarified. Both Diploma and B.Sc. qualified candidates have to obtain the following minimum eligibility marks for admission to Lateral Entry. For the MBC and DNC categories, a pass with a minimum average mark of 45 percent is required. B.Sc. For the Ph.D Degree in Mechanical Engineering, candidates must have a Master's Degree or any other qualification recognized as equivalent thereto in the fields of study notified from time to time by Anna University. Candidates should have the required qualification in the order of studies 10th, HSC, UG, and PG degree or its equivalent qualification. Alternatively, a Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or Technology of the University or any other qualification recognized as equivalent thereto in the fields of study with a minimum of 15 years of R and D Experience in National Research Laboratories or Public sector undertakings and with a minimum of three publications in referred impact factor journals or two approved international patents in the last five years is accepted. A minimum of 55 percent marks or a CGPA of 5.5 on a 10 point scale in the qualifying examination is required. In the case of SC, ST, or Differently-Abled candidates, 50 percent marks or a CGPA of 5.0 on a 10 point scale is required.

The Science Club at Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering and Architecture was established with the primary objective of inviting renowned scientists to share their experiences and inspire students to acquire scientific knowledge. By designing engaging activities, the club aims to introduce students to exciting science and technology projects that foster a deeper understanding of the scientific world.

The Science Club is an inclusive organization, open to all students, and comprises a group of enthusiastic individuals who are eager to explore the various branches of engineering, mathematics, and science. As one of the largest clubs in **MSAJCEA**, it is divided into three distinct sections: Physics, Chemistry, and General. The club's purpose is multifaceted, seeking to promote interest, understanding, and knowledge of science among college students and the local community.

One of the club's primary goals is to stimulate engineers' interest in learning science, thereby enhancing their academic achievement in science subjects. Through its activities, the club also aims to teach students how to apply their scientific knowledge in daily life, guiding them to develop independent, logical, and creative minds. To achieve this, the club organizes a variety of activities, including experiments in making electronic components, invisible ink, electroplating, biodiesels, fire writing, and creating venation of leaves.

To keep students informed, the club displays the latest news and day-to-day information about science on the notice board, ensuring that all engineers have access to the latest updates and developments in the scientific world.

The Science Club at Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering and Architecture operates under a set of guiding principles that serve as a foundation for developing engaging activities. These principles govern the design of the activities, which are centered around five key objectives. One of the primary activities offered by the Science Club is the Investigator program, which provides students with the opportunity to tackle real-world, science-based problems within a given scenario. This program allows students to work independently or in pairs/small groups, engaging in hands-on science experiments and activities that foster critical thinking and discussion about scientific concepts.

The scholarship amount is 10000 rupees per year, with 4883 scholarships for Tamil Nadu. Financial Assistance for Education to the wards of Beedi, Mine, and Cine workers, funded by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, requires an income of less than 10000 per month. B.Sc. Candidates must have a pass with prescribed minimum eligibility marks in any recognized Bachelor’s Degree in Science of minimum 3 years duration with 10 plus 2 plus 3 years pattern and studied core Mathematics as one of the subjects at degree level. Degree examinations or equivalent is required.
